title: The pictures the game draws on screen
target: Where the prompts, the card artwork and the animated crowd in TCG Card Shop Simulator come from, so what is on screen can be read for what it is.
version: no version stated by this build (see the sources page)
prerequisites: A shop with customers in it
A controller or keyboard if you want to compare prompts

steps.do: Read a prompt from the interactable's own list rather than from a global key map.
steps.because: an interactable carries a list of input displays, with a second list for controller-only displays (m_GameActionInputDisplayList, m_ControllerOnlyGameActionInputDisplayList)

steps.do: Expect a click and a hold to look different.
steps.because: the game ships a picture of a left mouse click and another for holding the button (LeftMouseClick, LeftMouseHold)

steps.do: Expect named keys, and a plain key picture when a key has no name.
steps.because: it ships a plain key picture as well as named key pictures covering control, tab and shift (KeyboardBtn, KeyboardBtn_Ctrl, KeyboardBtn_Tab, KeyboardBtn_Shift)

steps.do: Know that a card on screen is laid out by a settings object rather than by the card.
steps.because: a card is drawn by a settings object that holds its border, background, rarity and front pictures as lists and masks the art to a card shape (CardUISetting, CardUISettingData)

steps.do: Expect the colouring to come from the settings rather than from the art.
steps.because: the settings carry a background colour for a card without foil and a different one for a foil card, with separate colours for the evolution, play-effect and description backgrounds (cardBGColorNonFoil, cardBGColorFoil, evoBGColor, playEffectBGColor, descriptionBGColor)

steps.do: Know that a crowd can be animated from a baked set rather than a live rig.
steps.because: a baked set is built from a source prefab and an archetype and keeps the bones as a texture (BakedAnimationSet, sourcePrefab, archetype, boneTexture)

steps.do: Expect the bake to be laid out in blocks with a frame rate of its own.
steps.because: it is laid out in blocks with block and texture sizes and runs at a frame rate of its own (blockWidth, blockHeight, textureWidth, textureHeight)

steps.do: Know that a baked set can be inspected later.
steps.because: the set keeps its clips, CPU copies of the bone transforms and a bake log recorded with the set (boneTexture, clips, bakeLog)

commonMistakes: Expecting a controller prompt where only a keyboard one was set up.
Assuming the card's look lives on the card rather than in a settings object.
Reading a crowd's movement as one animation per character.
Treating a baked animation as something that cannot be looked into.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
